status: Unpublished release candidate. Not on npm, under this or any other name. Install from the versioned archive at https://zodiacs.org/examples/, whose SHA-256 is published beside it.

bundled.note: Engine 0.1.1-rc.16 and the site comparison are inlined into server.mjs. The engine was published to npm on 2026-10-01 under the next tag; the bundle is built from the archive whose SHA-256 is below, which npm's tarball matches. Bundling keeps one copy of the comparison rules.

comparison.note: The same module the browser tool at https://zodiacs.org/developers/compare/ runs.

computeApi.note: The hosted compute API's parsers and positions, events and sky-fact calculations, inlined into server.mjs, so get_positions, find_events and check_sky_fact return what POST https://zodiacs.org/api/v1/positions, /events and /sky-fact return for the same request, without a zone.

protocol.note: Revisions observed to negotiate against this server on the wire, one probe each. The official SDK client offers 2025-11-25.

schemas.note: Zodiacs-owned vocabulary, not an industry interoperability standard. The record and receipt schemas are drafts.

changedSince: rc.1 to rc.10, rc.14, rc.15, rc.16 and rc.16.1 remain unchanged as separate archives; there were no rc.11 to rc.13 archives. The engine is the same 0.1.1-rc.16, so every position, angle, cusp and comparison is rc.16's. New in rc.16.2: three tools, get_positions, find_events and check_sky_fact, which run the hosted compute API's own parsers and calculations, so each returns the compute API's body for the same request, with the same receipt and so the same cite.receipt; only cite.url names the tool. find_events finds sign ingresses, stations and new and full moons in a window of at most 92 days, and its receipt says its search is tested, not proven complete. check_sky_fact answers true, false or depends with the values that decide it; this adapter looks up no time zone, so it has no zone argument and reads a date as that day in every UTC offset in use today at once. Each new tool declares an output schema and the same read-only, closed-world annotations. The three existing tools' names and arguments are unchanged. The adapter itself is still not on npm.
